UMH.purpose: Minimize human friction while maximizing human capability under real-world constraints. Every subsystem, feature, phase, and architectural choice must serve this directive.
open_questions: Persistence architecture not locked — Postgres vs SQLite vs hybrid for MVP; vector store selection; event log schema; trace retention policy; backup strategy
Event model not defined — the spine needs a formal event model (SignalReceived, InterpretationCompleted, etc.) to avoid procedural spaghetti
Authorization model incomplete — governance modes defined but not the policy schema (risk classes, approval channels, user confirmation format, default deny rules)
Capability registry schema needs full formalization beyond the conceptual contract
Adapter contract details missing — manifest, input/output validation, dry-run support, rollback, observability hooks, idempotency, credential handling
Runtime boundary not decided — what UMH does directly vs delegates; rule exists but specific boundaries undefined
Testing doctrine absent — folder exists but no test strategy (protocol validation, governance denial, trace completeness, replay, end-to-end spine)
Security requires more explicit treatment — secrets manager, least privilege, sandboxing, command allow/deny, file path restrictions, credential scope
Human feedback UX not designed — structured format for was-useful/outcome-achieved/accepted-rejected-edited/what-changed/why-wrong
Tab 10 references tabs 1 and 11 which are numbered differently than what appears — possible tab reordering or missing tabs between iterations
Roadmap phase numbers changed between tabs (76-108 in tab 5, then 76-110 in tab 6) — indicates roadmap was revised but not reconciled
No mention of LLM cost management strategy despite extensive adapter/capability system
Simulation/counterfactual system described in tabs 4-5 but no implementation approach defined

EOS.purpose: AI-native business operating system that enables founders and operators to run one or more companies through unified organizational structure, role-based dashboards, workflows/SOPs, agentic execution, strategic intelligence, memory/knowledge systems, governance/approvals, and cross-platform integration with CreatorOS and LYFEOS.
EOS.target_user: Solo founders and owner-operators running one or more companies who need structure, execution leverage, and AI assistance without bloated teams. Secondary: small teams (2-10 people). Future: enterprise teams, AI-first solo operators.
EOS.business_model: SaaS subscription model. Part of the Lyfe Institute product ladder (Initiate Arena is the current entry product). North star: $10K/month net profit, scalable. Long-term: 11-figure empire by 50. Multi-tenant platform serving multiple founders/companies. Revenue from subscription access to the AI-native business OS. Future: skill marketplace, enterprise licensing.

prd_quality.notes: The end-state PRD is exceptionally comprehensive in WHAT the system should do (28 sections covering every conceivable subsystem) and the universal business primitive taxonomy (Tab 11) is genuinely novel and well-structured. The MVP PRD is well-scoped with clear non-goals. However, specificity drops significantly when moving from 'what' to 'how' — there are no wireframes, no API contracts, no specific UI component specs, no data flow diagrams. Actionability suffers because much of the document is aspirational end-state vision mixed with current-system audits, making it hard to extract buildable user stories. The biological/Reality Mimicry metaphors (Tab 12) are intellectually rich but add no engineering specificity. The strongest actionable content is the MVP data model (Tab 1 section 11), the universal primitive taxonomy (Tab 11), and the EA gap analysis (Tab 9). The weakest areas are pricing/monetization (completely absent), UX specifics (no wireframes or interaction patterns), and competitive positioning. The document would benefit from separating the vision document from the buildable spec — right now they're interleaved across multiple tabs with significant redundancy (End-State PRD appears twice in Tab 1, substrate audit appears 3 times in Tab 15, Reality Mimicry content duplicated in Tab 12).

CreatorOS.purpose: The command center for modern creators — a single platform combining cross-platform content distribution, community hosting (Discord-like), course creation (Teachable-like), digital product sales (Gumroad-like), and a built-in marketplace for discovery. For consumers, a unified feed experience aggregating all content from followed creators across platforms.
CreatorOS.target_user: Primary: Creators (Emerging 1K-50K followers, Established 50K-500K, Creator Businesses 500K+). Secondary: Consumers (Superfans, Learners, Community Members). Tertiary: UGC Creators (subtype), Advertisers.
CreatorOS.business_model: SaaS subscription tiers: Starter (Free, 3 platforms, 1 community, 1 course, 8% transaction fee), Pro ($29/mo, unlimited, 5% fee), Business ($99/mo, team seats, API, white-label, 3% fee), Enterprise (custom). Revenue streams: SaaS subscriptions (primary), transaction fees (3-8% on sales), marketplace promotion (paid placement), Consumer Pro (future: ad-free, offline). Creator payouts via Stripe Connect, weekly, $25 minimum, 135+ countries, instant payouts for verified creators (1% fee).

prd_quality.notes: The document is extremely comprehensive in breadth — 12 full systems defined with detailed feature tables, data models, API endpoints, and infrastructure specs. However, it suffers from significant redundancy and internal contradictions due to being built iteratively through conversation. The same concepts (MVP scope, tech stack, database schema, API spec) are defined 2-4 times with minor variations, making it unclear which version is canonical. The full-version PRD (Systems 1-22) is well-structured and thorough. The MVP definition is inconsistent across its multiple appearances. Tab 8's ecosystem architecture is visionary but entirely conceptual — no implementation contracts. The Build Guide (pos 674944+) is the most actionable section but references yet another auth provider (Clerk) that contradicts the main PRD. Overall: strong vision, strong feature definition, but needs a single canonical pass to resolve contradictions, pick definitive tech choices, and consolidate the 3+ MVP definitions into one.

LyfeOS.purpose: Personal Life Operating System (PLOS) that treats human life as a stateful, evolving system. Unifies identity development, execution, reflection, AI assistance, and long-term progression into one coherent platform.
LyfeOS.target_user: Phase 1: Founders, executives, operators managing complex multi-domain lives; high-agency individuals already doing the work but lacking system coherence; users juggling 5+ productivity/wellness tools; self-directed learners. Phase 2+: Coaches, consultants, business owners, leadership teams, creative professionals.
LyfeOS.business_model: Subscription SaaS. Phase 1 targets 100 daily users (free/beta). Phase 2: 500 users. Phase 3: 2,000 users. Phase 4: 10K+ users with enterprise/team tiers. Revenue targets: $1M+ ARR in Phase 4. Coach/client relationship mode and white-label options planned. LTV:CAC ratio target 3:1. Part of broader Lyfe Institute ecosystem (LYFEOS + EntrepreneurOS + CreatorOS).

prd_quality.notes: Extremely thorough product specification - one of the most detailed PRDs seen. Every onboarding question, every data model field, every hex color code, every XP calculation formula is specified. Specificity is exceptional with exact SQL schemas, component styles, and animation timings. However, actionability is lowered by: (1) significant version conflicts between PRD v1.0 (4 tabs, 3 models) and v2.0 (5 tabs, 5 models) coexisting in the same document, (2) timeline inconsistencies across sections, (3) massive content repetition across tabs (the same onboarding spec appears 3+ times in different formats), (4) missing error handling, offline behavior, and operational specs, (5) Tabs 52-53 describe an aspirational ecosystem architecture that is conceptual only with no implementation path. The document would benefit from a single canonical MVP spec with all conflicts resolved. The isolated MVP at lyfeos.net demonstrates that the core spec IS executable - the implementation proved the MVP PRD works. The ecosystem architecture (LYFEOS + EntrepreneurOS + CreatorOS on shared kernel) is compelling but currently at whiteboard stage only.
